previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of CABG and mitral valve replacement, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for a left lower extremity angiogram due to a nonhealing foot ulcer. The procedure was performed via the right femoral artery and showed patent iliac and femoral arteries with non-significant stenoses, but occlusion of the posterior tibial artery and poor hindfoot perfusion. No intervention was performed. She tolerated the procedure well, resumed her home medications except for warfarin, which she restarted the night after discharge. She was discharged home the following day with wound care instructions, activity restrictions, and plans for outpatient vascular follow-up with ABI/PVR testing.
